meta.titre: The electromagnetic spectrum: waves, wavelengths and uses
meta.sous_theme: Members of the spectrum, wave equation, uses and dangers

sections.contenu_markdown: When you listen to a radio in Garoua, warm food in a microwave oven, switch the channel with a TV remote, get a bone X-ray at the hospital, or put on sunscreen, you meet members of the same family of waves. They are called electromagnetic waves and together they form the electromagnetic spectrum. At the GCE, you are asked to name members in order, give a range of wavelength, state what they have in common, use $v = f\lambda$, and link a use to a property.

items: A wave has a wavelength $\lambda$ (metres), a frequency $f$ (hertz) and a speed $v$.
A transverse wave vibrates at right angles to the direction in which it travels.

sections.titre: Members of the spectrum and the wave equation
sections.contenu_markdown:
**Properties common to all electromagnetic waves.** They are transverse waves; they can travel through a vacuum; they all travel at the same speed in a vacuum, $c = 3.0\times10^{8}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; they carry energy; they can be reflected, refracted and diffracted. They differ in wavelength and frequency, and in the effect they have on matter.

**Wave equation.** For any wave

$$v = f\lambda$$

and for electromagnetic waves in a vacuum (or air) $c = f\lambda$. So when the frequency is larger the wavelength is smaller: $\lambda = c/f$.

**The spectrum** in order of **decreasing wavelength** (increasing frequency and energy):

| Member | Approximate wavelength | Example of use |
|---|---|---|
| Radio waves | more than $0.1\,\mathrm{m}$ | radio and TV broadcasting |
| Microwaves | $1\,\mathrm{mm}$ to $0.1\,\mathrm{m}$ | cooking, mobile phones, satellite links |
| Infrared | $700\,\mathrm{nm}$ to $1\,\mathrm{mm}$ | remote controls, heaters, thermal cameras |
| Visible light | $400$ to $700\,\mathrm{nm}$ | vision, photography, optical fibres |
| Ultraviolet | $10$ to $400\,\mathrm{nm}$ | sterilising water, detecting forged banknotes |
| X-rays | $0.01$ to $10\,\mathrm{nm}$ | medical imaging, security scanners |
| Gamma rays | less than $0.01\,\mathrm{nm}$ | sterilising equipment, treating cancer |

Here $1\,\mathrm{nm} = 10^{-9}\,\mathrm{m}$. The boundaries are approximate and neighbouring regions overlap. Red light has the longest wavelength in the visible region and violet the shortest.

variantes.quand_utiliser: when the frequency or wavelength is given and the other is needed
variantes.contenu_markdown: Write $\lambda = c/f$ or $f = c/\lambda$ and use $c = 3.0\times10^{8}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. Convert MHz to Hz ($1\,\mathrm{MHz} = 10^{6}\,\mathrm{Hz}$) and nm to m before substituting. Compare the wavelength found with the table to name the region. Because the speed is constant, the time for a signal to travel a distance $d$ is $t = d/c$.

variantes.quand_utiliser: when asked to relate a use to a property of the named wave
variantes.contenu_markdown: Radio waves have long wavelengths that diffract around hills and are reflected by the ionosphere. Microwaves are absorbed by water molecules, which heats food, and pass through the atmosphere, so they are used for satellites. Infrared is emitted by hot objects and heats the skin. Ultraviolet makes some materials fluoresce and kills bacteria. X-rays pass through soft tissue but are absorbed by bones. Gamma rays penetrate deeply and kill living cells, so they can sterilise equipment and treat tumours.

The danger increases with the frequency (energy) of the wave. Microwaves can heat body tissue. Too much infrared causes burns. Ultraviolet damages skin cells and eyes and can cause skin cancer. X-rays and gamma rays are ionising: they can damage cells and cause cancer, so exposure is kept short and workers use lead shielding.

sections.enonce_markdown: A radio station transmits on a frequency of $60\,\mathrm{MHz}$. The speed of electromagnetic waves in air is $3.0\times10^{8}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. (a) Calculate the wavelength of the waves and name the region of the spectrum. (b) A town is $150\,\mathrm{km}$ from the transmitter. How long does a signal take to reach it?

etapes.justification: The wave equation needs the frequency in hertz.

etapes.action: Name the region of the spectrum.
etapes.justification: Compare $\lambda$ with the table: a wavelength greater than $0.1\,\mathrm{m}$ is in the radio region.

etapes.action: Convert the distance to metres and find the travel time.
etapes.justification: The signal travels at the constant speed $c$, so $t = d/c$.

sections.conclusion_markdown: The wavelength is $5.0\,\mathrm{m}$ (radio waves), and the signal takes $5.0\times10^{-4}\,\mathrm{s}$, that is $0.50\,\mathrm{ms}$, to reach the town.

items.erreur_markdown: Gamma rays travel faster than radio waves because they have more energy.
items.pourquoi_faux: All electromagnetic waves travel at the same speed in a vacuum, $3.0\times10^{8}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. They differ in frequency, wavelength and energy.
items.correction_markdown: Same speed $c$; higher frequency and shorter wavelength for gamma rays.

items.erreur_markdown: Ultraviolet has a longer wavelength than visible light.
items.pourquoi_faux: The prefix "ultra" means beyond violet, which is the shortest visible wavelength. Ultraviolet waves therefore have shorter wavelengths (and higher frequency) than visible light.
items.correction_markdown: Order by decreasing wavelength: radio, microwave, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-ray, gamma.

items.erreur_markdown: Sound waves are part of the electromagnetic spectrum.
items.pourquoi_faux: Sound is a longitudinal mechanical wave that needs a medium and cannot travel through a vacuum. Electromagnetic waves are transverse and need no medium.
items.correction_markdown: Say that electromagnetic waves can travel through a vacuum, and sound cannot.

items.erreur_markdown: A microwave oven heats the food only on the outside because microwaves cannot go inside.
items.pourquoi_faux: Microwaves penetrate a few centimetres into the food and are absorbed by water molecules, which heats the food directly. Heat then spreads towards the centre by conduction.
items.correction_markdown: Microwaves are absorbed by water in the food, which makes the molecules vibrate and heats the food.

items.erreur_markdown: Calculating $\lambda = c/f$ with $f = 60$ for a $60\,\mathrm{MHz}$ station.
items.pourquoi_faux: The frequency must be in hertz. With $f = 60$ the wavelength is $5\times10^{6}\,\mathrm{m}$, a million times too large.

items.enonce_markdown: Arrange these members of the electromagnetic spectrum in order of increasing wavelength: infrared, gamma rays, radio waves, visible light, X-rays, ultraviolet, microwaves.
items.solution_markdown: Shortest wavelength first: **gamma rays, X-rays, ultraviolet, visible light, infrared, microwaves, radio waves**. All of them travel at the same speed, $3.0\times10^{8}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, in a vacuum.

items.enonce_markdown: Green light has a wavelength of $5.0\times10^{-7}\,\mathrm{m}$ in air. Calculate its frequency. Express the wavelength in nanometres.
items.solution_markdown:
Formula: $f = \dfrac{c}{\lambda}$

Substitution: $f = \dfrac{3.0\times10^{8}}{5.0\times10^{-7}}$

Result: **$f = 6.0\times10^{14}\,\mathrm{Hz}$**.

Wavelength in nanometres: $5.0\times10^{-7}\,\mathrm{m} = 500\times10^{-9}\,\mathrm{m}$, which is **$500\,\mathrm{nm}$**, inside the visible range of $400$ to $700\,\mathrm{nm}$.

items.enonce_markdown: (a) A radiation has a frequency of $6.0\times10^{17}\,\mathrm{Hz}$. Calculate its wavelength and name the region of the spectrum. (b) A microwave communication link uses waves of frequency $1.5\times10^{10}\,\mathrm{Hz}$. Calculate their wavelength and name the region. (c) Give one use and one danger of the radiation in (a).
items.solution_markdown:
(a) $\lambda = \dfrac{c}{f} = \dfrac{3.0\times10^{8}}{6.0\times10^{17}}$, so **$\lambda = 5.0\times10^{-10}\,\mathrm{m}$** ($0.50\,\mathrm{nm}$). This lies between $0.01$ and $10\,\mathrm{nm}$: **X-rays**.

(b) $\lambda = \dfrac{3.0\times10^{8}}{1.5\times10^{10}}$, so **$\lambda = 0.020\,\mathrm{m}$** ($2.0\,\mathrm{cm}$). This lies between $1\,\mathrm{mm}$ and $0.1\,\mathrm{m}$: **microwaves**.

(c) Use: X-rays show broken bones because they pass through soft tissue and are absorbed by bone. Danger: they are ionising radiation, which can damage cells and cause cancer, so exposure must be limited and shielded.

items_markdown: All electromagnetic waves are **transverse**, travel in a **vacuum**, and have the same speed $c = 3.0\times10^{8}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ there.
Order of **decreasing wavelength**: radio, microwave, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-ray, gamma. Frequency and energy increase in the opposite direction.
Wave equation: $c = f\lambda$. Convert MHz and nm to Hz and m first.
Each use depends on a property: microwaves are absorbed by water, X-rays are absorbed by bones, gamma rays kill cells, ultraviolet kills bacteria.
The higher the frequency, the greater the danger: X-rays and gamma rays are ionising.
